report:
# Research Findings: Does Flu Vaccination Cause Alzheimer's Disease?

**Bottom line: The claim is false. Rigorous evidence points the opposite direction—flu vaccination is associated with *reduced*, not increased, Alzheimer's risk.**

**Origin of the claim:** This idea traces largely to Hugh Fudenberg, a retired immunologist who in 1997 asserted (without published peer-reviewed data) that receiving five or more annual flu shots increases Alzheimer's risk tenfold, allegedly due to mercury/aluminum in vaccines. This claim was popularized by figures like Bill Maher and has circulated on social media ever since. Fact-checkers and medical reviewers have consistently found no clinical studies supporting it (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/H._Hugh_Fudenberg; https://www.kwch.com/content/news/FF12-Flu-shot-post-circulating-social-media-isnt-true-471352374.html). The Alzheimer's Association explicitly lists "flu shots increase Alzheimer's risk" as a myth, also noting the related aluminum-causes-Alzheimer's theory has been debunked (https://www.alz.org/alzheimers-dementia/what-is-alzheimers/myths).

**What actual research shows:** Multiple large cohort studies find the opposite association. A study of ~935,000 vaccinated vs. unvaccinated matched patients found flu vaccination linked to a ~40% *reduced* risk of Alzheimer's (PMC9484126, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9484126/). A 2026 Neurology study of nearly 200,000 older adults found high-dose flu vaccine further reduced Alzheimer's risk compared to standard dose, especially in women (https://www.neurology.org/doi/10.1212/WNL.0000000000214782). UK Biobank data similarly showed reduced dementia risk with vaccination (nature.com/articles/s41541-024-00841-z).

**Caveat:** These are observational/associational studies, not proof of causation for protection, but they directly contradict the harm claim and are far more methodologically rigorous than the original unsupported assertion.
